title: On Wagstaff primes in the $k$-Lucas number sequence
summary: A Wagstaff prime is a prime number of the form $(2^{\mathfrak{p}}+1)/3$, where $\mathfrak{p}$ is an odd prime. Let $(L_n^{(k)})_{n\geq 2-k}$ be the $k$-Lucas number sequence defined by the recurrence relation $ L_n^{(k)} = L_{n-1}^{(k)} + \cdots + L_{n-k}^{(k)}$, for all $n \ge 2$, with initial terms \( L_0^{(k)} = 2 \) and \( L_1^{(k)} = 1 \) for all \( k \ge 2 \), and \( L_{2-k}^{(k)} = \cdots = L_{-1}^{(k)} = 0 \) for \( k \ge 3 \).
